definition: Cognitive penetrability is the idea that higher-level mental states, such as beliefs, expectations, attention, or memory, can shape what a person actually perceives. In a broad sense this includes top-down influences through attention and memory, while in a narrower sense it means flexible high-level factors directly change the percept itself, a claim the source says remains debated and not strongly evidenced for clear visual perception.

reasons: The definition includes examples of “higher-level mental states” such as “beliefs” and “expectations,” but the packet only explicitly discusses “attention” and “memory” (and mentions other unspecified “high-level factors”) rather than beliefs or expectations.
